tagline: A 15th-century Ottoman fortress at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus — dramatic views, a charming village below, and one of Istanbul's most romantic spots.

items.name: Hisarüstü Çay Bahçeleri
items.description: Tea gardens on the hillside above the fortress with extraordinary Bosphorus views. A hidden gem that locals treasure.
items.tip: The gardens above the fortress are not signposted — walk up the steep road behind the main entrance and keep going until you find them.

items.name: Rumeli Hisarı Village Cafés
items.description: A small cluster of cafés in the village below the fortress, popular with Boğaziçi University students and locals.

items.name: Köfeci Ramiz
items.description: A classic neighbourhood köfte restaurant near the fortress that has been feeding locals for decades. Simple and excellent.

items.name: Rumeli Hisarı Kalesi
items.description: The great Ottoman fortress built by Mehmed II in 1452 to control the Bosphorus before the conquest of Constantinople. Walk the towers and walls.
items.tip: Climb to the top tower for the best Bosphorus view in Istanbul — the narrowest crossing point visible below.

items.name: Bebek to Rumeli Hisarı Coastal Walk
items.description: A 20-minute waterfront walk north from Bebek to the fortress. One of Istanbul's most scenic short walks.

tips: Best reached by bus from Beşiktaş along the Bosphorus coastal road (25E or 22 series buses).
Combine with Bebek (20-min walk south) — start in Bebek, walk to the fortress, take the bus back.
The fortress hosts occasional summer concerts in its courtyard — check the events calendar.
The Boğaziçi University campus is just above the village and worth exploring for its Bosphorus views.
